To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt is associated with increased CT scan findings in patients presenting to the ED with IIH.

the presence of an intracranial shunt in patients with IIH is not associated with a change in the diagnostic CT findings, and that the CT scan is not useful in the emergency department evaluation of patients with suspected IIH.

computed tomography (CT) was not associated with a significant difference in clinical decision making for shunted patients with idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) presenting to the emergency department (ED), and that CT was associated with a significantly longer ED length of stay (LOS).
